points.heading: Week overview
points.body:
This week we learned to narrate time in Spanish: sometimes the verb travels alone (one word), sometimes with haber (two words: **helper** + **already-done** form).

## Key idea

## More examples
One-word clock: **canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría**.
Two-word clock: **he cantado / había comido / habré vivido / habría terminado**.
Choose: «Yesterday I **finished**» (one closed word) vs «I **have finished** already» (two words).
Story mix: «I **was reading** when the phone **rang**.»

Practice: Now it's your turn. Calmly explain to someone at home the difference between canté and he cantado with your own example.

Common mistake: Repeating hard labels without building a real sentence.

points.heading: Overview: one word
points.body:
The five **one-word** times are five stations on the same train: canto, cantaba, canté, cantaré, cantaría.

## Key idea

## More examples
One-word clock: **canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría**.
Two-word clock: **he cantado / había comido / habré vivido / habría terminado**.
Choose: «Yesterday I **finished**» (one closed word) vs «I **have finished** already» (two words).
Story mix: «I **was reading** when the phone **rang**.»

Practice: Now it's your turn. Recite the I-forms and after each one say the «when» in a short phrase.

Common mistake: Using cantaba for a closed yesterday fact.

points.heading: Overview: two words
points.body:
The **two-word** path always has the same shape: **helper** haber + participle (-ado/-ido). he cantado is the clearest starting example.

## Key idea

## More examples
One-word clock: **canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría**.
Two-word clock: **he cantado / había comido / habré vivido / habría terminado**.
Choose: «Yesterday I **finished**» (one closed word) vs «I **have finished** already» (two words).
Story mix: «I **was reading** when the phone **rang**.»

Practice: Now it's your turn. Write three sentences with he / había / habría + cantado as three moments of one story.

Common mistake: Changing the participle by person.

points.heading: Overview: choosing
points.body:
Today we will walk through this idea step by step. To choose, return to the three questions: closed moment, result until now, or background/habit.

## Key idea

## More examples
One-word clock: **canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría**.
Two-word clock: **he cantado / había comido / habré vivido / habría terminado**.
Choose: «Yesterday I **finished**» (one closed word) vs «I **have finished** already» (two words).
Story mix: «I **was reading** when the phone **rang**.»

Practice: Now it's your turn. Sort five of your sentences into those three groups and explain one aloud.

Common mistake: Choosing at random without looking at time words (ayer, ya, cuando…).

points.heading: Synthesis
points.body:
Today we will walk through this idea step by step. If you can build an example, you understand the heart of it. Long names can wait; first master the story: one word or two.

## Key idea

## More examples
One-word clock: **canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría**.
Two-word clock: **he cantado / había comido / habré vivido / habría terminado**.
Choose: «Yesterday I **finished**» (one closed word) vs «I **have finished** already» (two words).
Story mix: «I **was reading** when the phone **rang**.»

Practice: Now it's your turn. Write a four-sentence mini-paragraph using at least one one-word time and one two-word time.

Common mistake: Memorizing lists without writing sentences.

lesson.summary: This lesson teaches review spanish indicative tenses. Understand the central idea first, then explore it, practice it, and check a common mistake.
lesson.memoryPhrase: One word: **canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría**. Two words: helper **haber** + already-done form (**he cantado**).

questions.prompt: Which Spanish form shows an action happening now?
Which form tells about a finished action yesterday?

choices: A repeated or ongoing past action.
questions.answer: A repeated or ongoing past action.

questions.prompt: What two parts make a compound tense?
choices: A form of haber and a participle.
questions.answer: A form of haber and a participle.

questions.prompt: In «he cantado», which word is the participle?
Why should «comido» stay the same in «hemos comido»?
choices: It is always a future word.
The participle does not become plural for the subject.
questions.answer: The participle does not become plural for the subject.

questions.prompt: Busca en el punto 1 («Week overview») y escribe entre comillas las palabras exactas donde la clase habla de esto: Yesterday I **finished**. Luego explica con tus palabras qué entendiste.
Copia entre comillas la frase exacta del punto 2 («Overview: one word») que mejor resume la idea principal. Después explica por qué esa frase es importante.
En el punto 3 («Overview: two words»), encuentra y copia entre comillas las palabras exactas relacionadas con: Yesterday I **finished**. Explica qué significa esa idea en la clase de hoy.
Escribe entre comillas una cita exacta del punto 4 («Overview: choosing») que puedas usar para enseñarle a un compañero esta idea. Luego explica la cita con tus propias palabras.
